a: Combined p-value (physical uranium uptake parameter) trajectories for enamel and dentine illustrating the relative goodness-of-fit of uranium-uptake histories over the modelled time interval. The enamel curve indicates a broader temporal sensitivity, while dentine exhibits steeper p-value responses reflecting higher susceptibility to uranium migration. b: Normalised uranium-uptake curves for enamel (red) and dentine (green) showing contrasting U-uptake kinetics, with enamel characterised by delayed uptake and dentine by more rapid early incorporation. c: Frequency distribution of modelled ages generated under the US-ESR age model, illustrating the central tendency and dispersion of the Monte-Carlo age simulations used to derive the final age estimate, d H. erectus tooth from Baxian that was dated using US-ESR techniques (Supplementary Information 6).

In a recent development, a and b are the dating results (n = 43) as separate age estimates in kyr for the five dating techniques modelled according to Oxcal and applied to the sediments and fossils of Naxian (a) and Baxian (b) caves. Data are presented as mean values +/− SD. The techniques are colour coded according to the legend and organised into the unit in which they were sampled from – the flowstone, breccia or underlying clay. Some of the techniques represent minimum ages (such as the US ages on teeth) and contain a colour coded arrow pointing the right, while other represent maximum ages such as the pIR-IRSL single aliquot dating of feldspars and contain a colour coded arrow pointing the left. The thick black horizontal boxes with dashed lines represent the boundary ages (and errors) estimated by the modelling. The boundary ages quoted represent the upper and lower age ranges for the breccia units in both caves. c and d are the dating results (n = 43) as separate age estimates in kyr modelling according to Chronomodel for the same five dating techniques. Data are presented as mean values +/− SD. The individual sample events have been organised into three phases; breccia deposition (including fossil and sediment ages), overlying flowstone precipitation and underlying clay deposition with each phase represented by a different plot. The timescale goes from more recent on the right (50 ka written as -50000) to oldest on the left (400 ka written as -400000). For Baxian (c) we have used the age uncertainty at 2 σ (95%) of the fossil teeth dated using US-ESR (H. erectus and Pongo), resulting in an age of 324-184 ka. For Naxian (d), the fossils are all dated using US only so represent minimum ages, so instead we have used the period between the overlying flowstone (as the minimum age) and the youngest soda straw in the breccia (as the maximum age) both at 2 σ (95%) uncertainty to constrain the age of breccia deposition at 319-241 ka. The use of Chronomodel compared to Oxcal has accentuated similar events and reduced the younger age uncertainty by around 20 kyr. The overlapping uncertainty between the two caves has been used to represent a Homo erectus presence at some point between 324-184 ka.

a Taxon-specific δ13Ccarbon source values in relation to vegetation type. δ13Ccarbon source (plant-equivalent values; ‰ VPDB at Baxian (324-184) and Naxian (319-241 ka). Shaded background areas indicate ecological zones: dense canopy forest (dark green), C3 vegetation (light green), and C4 grassland (yellow). The unshaded interval between C3 and C4 represents the C3–C4 intermediate zone. This framework allows direct comparison of faunal isotopic signatures against expected vegetation regimes. A large proportion of taxa from both sites fall within the dense canopy forest zone, supporting the interpretation of closed-canopy rainforest environments. The H. erectus values (red stars) fall within the C3 forest domain and plot at the boundary between dense canopy forest and more open C3 vegetation. b Vegetation zone proportions at hominin-bearing sites in Southeast Asia and South China. Proportional distribution of faunal δ13Ccarbon source values assigned to vegetation zones (dense canopy C3, open C3, C3–C4 intermediate, and C4). Bars show the relative contributions of each zone across six hominin-bearing sites: Trinil4, Sangiran5, Cobra Cave34,73, Duoi U’Oi74, Lida Ajer45,75, Baxian and Naxian. Baxian and Naxian are dominated by C3 signals, with substantial contributions from dense canopy vegetation, while Trinil and Sangiran show higher proportions of intermediate and C4 values, reflecting more open habitats. Lida Ajer is strongly weighted toward dense canopy values, consistent with closed rainforest settings. Together, these results illustrate marked ecological contrasts between late H. erectus contexts in China and Javanese sites, as well as affinities between Naxian and the rainforest environment of early H. sapiens at Lida Ajer75,76,77.

Recent findings suggest that a Trace element distribution maps of the Baxian H. erectus tooth. LA-ICP-MS elemental maps showing the distribution of (i) 7Li/43Ca, (ii) 88Sr/43Ca, (iii) 138Ba/43Ca, and (iv) 238U/43Ca ratios normalised to calcium across a longitudinal section of the tooth. All maps show both enamel (upper/left portion, blue-green colours) and dentine (lower/right portion, predominantly dark red). The colour scales are optimised to visualise variation within the enamel tissue. Dark red areas in the dentine for Sr, Ba, and U maps indicate significantly elevated concentrations due to post-depositional diagenetic uptake from the burial environment, rendering these tissues unsuitable for life history reconstruction. In contrast, the enamel tissue displays lower concentrations and visible banding patterns, particularly Ba/Ca, and Sr/Ca maps, which reflect biogenic signals. The U/Ca map clearly illustrates the extent of diagenetic alteration, with the highest concentrations in dentine and at the enamel-dentine junction (EDJ), demonstrating the vulnerability of dental tissues to post-depositional elemental exchange. The Li/Ca map demonstrates elevated concentrations in both tissues with distinct banding in the enamel. All measurements were obtained using LA-ICP-MS with 40 μm spot size and Ca-normalization to account for matrix effects. b Strontium isotope ratio profiles across H. erectus tooth enamel from Baxian and Naxian caves. LA-MC-ICP-MS 87Sr/86Sr ratio profiles measured along linear transects across tooth enamel from (i) BAX-1 from Baxian Cave, and (ii) NX-A1, (iii) NX-B1, and (iv) NX-B2 from Naxian Cave. The x-axis represents distance in mm along the ablation transect from the cervical region toward the cusp, corresponding to the temporal sequence of enamel formation from early to late childhood. The y-axis shows 87Sr/86Sr ratios, with variation reflecting changes in geological substrate accessed through diet and drinking water during tooth formation. All four individuals exhibit substantial intra-tooth variation in 87Sr/86Sr ratios that exceeds analytical uncertainty, indicating mobility between geologically distinct regions or consumption of resources from multiple locations during childhood. BAX-1 shows 87Sr/86Sr ratios ranging from 0.7110 to 0.7220, while the Naxian specimens display overlapping ranges: NX-A1 (0.7115-0.7165), NX-B1 (0.7095-0.7165), and NX-B2 (0.7100-0.7160). The observed variation patterns provide evidence for landscape mobility of late Middle Pleistocene H. erectus populations in southern China. c Strontium isoscape and geographic assignment probabilities for H. erectus mobility in southern China and northern Southeast Asia. (i) Regional-scale strontium isoscape showing predicted bioavailable 87Sr/86Sr ratios across southern China, northern Vietnam, northern Laos, and adjacent regions. Colours indicate 87Sr/86Sr values ranging from 0.710 (dark blue) to 0.725 (pink), with the Baxian/Naxian cave sites marked by a white dot. Major cities (Hanoi, Lào Cai, Guilin) are shown for geographic reference. (ii) Prediction uncertainty map for the regional isoscape, showing standard error of predicted 87Sr/86Sr values ranging from 0.004 (yellow, low uncertainty) to 0.016 (purple, high uncertainty). (iii) Local-scale isoscape focused on a 400 km × 400 km region centred on the Baxian/Naxian sites, with scale bar representing 50 km. (iv) Prediction uncertainty map for the local isoscape (v-vii) Geographic assignment probability maps for three representative 87Sr/86Sr values observed in H. erectus tooth enamel: (v) Seq1 = 0.714, representing average values for NX-A1 and lower values in NX-B2, showing high assignment probabilities (yellow-green) concentrated within 30-50 km of the cave sites in limestone karst terrain; (vi) Seq2 = 0.719, representing transitional values observed in multiple specimens, showing assignment probabilities extending southward ~150-250 km toward the Red River valley region; (vii) Seq3 = 0.724, representing the most radiogenic values observed (particularly in BAX-1), showing assignment probabilities concentrated in the Red River valley foothills approximately 250 km south of the caves and near Lào Cai to the west, with very low probabilities in the local cave area (dark purple). The progressive southward shift in assignment probabilities from Seq1 to Seq3 indicates long-distance mobility of late H. erectus individuals between the local karst uplands and distant regions up to 250 km away during childhood tooth formation. All isoscapes generated using random forest machine learning based on33 global bioavailable strontium database.

Xabi Alonso had been clear that he wanted his Chelsea team to match Leeds physically and mentally in the spirit of this historically feisty fixture.

What he got in the end, though, was yet more evidence that this young team are there for the taking by those who want to take the game to them.

Leeds were sharper and nastier in every aspect today, and while Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, it came as no surprise to see Daniel Farke’s men snap back to equalise before running away with the game with such ferocity that Alonso’s future will, for the first time, come under some scrutiny.

There were boos at the break with the score level, but Leeds firmly on top, and the shower of condemnation that followed the full-time whistle vocalised in the clearest terms that Alonso is under pressure.

Alonso’s Blues started the season ferociously and looked like they could challenge for major honours, but Chelsea supporters have been here before.

They were always going to need more than a few exhilarating attacking displays to nail their names to the mast of a title challenge, and so it has proved.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Four 3/10s as Palmer anonymous.

Dismal Chelsea well beaten by Leeds as scrutiny on Alonso grows.

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

Chelsea are nowhere near runaway leaders Arsenal, and they are once again looking over their shoulders at sides who are less well-resourced but more tactically defined and mentally resolute.

Leeds dominated both boxes and were first to every ball, bullying Chelsea’s defence just as Sunderland and Brian Brobbey had before the international break.

Lessons have not been learned from last week, from last season or, frankly, any point of the BlueCo ownership. Chelsea as a team, while not short on quality, remain short of leaders.

They have looked to shoehorn young men into positions of responsibility, and this is the inevitable result. Teams with nous, experience and bite will continue to see Stamford Bridge as a challenge they can scale.

This was Leeds’ first win in this corner of west London since the turn of the millennium, the latest in a long list of teams to head to a formerly impenetrable Stamford Bridge and make history.

Chelsea rarely have answers for teams who seek to raise the temperature of the game. When the game becomes stretched, Chelsea become increasingly erratic and tempestuous.

It has been revealed that it is in these moments that the typically composed Alonso must do more to change the tide. His changes this afternoon came too late and made no difference. Leeds were in control of the game and the scoreline when Alonso turned to his bench just past the hour mark.

During his introductory press conference over the summer, Alonso was reluctant to say he believed he would get time to instil his ideas. His pessimism appears well placed because, just 11 games into the season, the pressure is ramping up.

Arsenal have been handed a huge injury scare after David Raya was forced off in the second-half of their Premier League clash against Newcastle.

The Gunners, who led at the break, were held to a 2-2 draw at St James’ Park as a resilient Newcastle fought their way back into the contest.

While chasing an equaliser, Raya was involved in an innocuous coming together with William Osula in the penalty area.

The Spaniard appeared to be in real pain as he clutched his left arm, using his shirt as a makeshift sling as he left the pitch to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was visibly distressed and at one stage appeared close to tears as he made his way off, sparking huge concern for the Gunners.

The 31-year-old has grown into a crucial figure at Arsenal, vital in their Premier League success last season having established himself as the best goalkeeper in the league.

Speaking after the draw, Arteta admitted the sight of his shot stopper in pain was ‘not good news’ with Raya to undergo an MRI scan on Sunday.

‘Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news,’ Arteta noted in his post-match press conference.

‘He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Third-placed Paris FC welcome Angers SCO to the Stade Jean Bouin in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with kick-off at 3pm local time.
  • The hosts have won four and drawn one of their five home league games, while the visitors are winless in five and sit 17th after Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 21 Nov 2026 12:38.

Third-placed Paris FC welcome Angers SCO to the Stade Jean Bouin in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with kick-off at 3pm local time.

The hosts have won four and drawn one of their five home league games, while the visitors are winless in five and sit 17th after Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday.

Paris FC have taken 20 points from 10 league games, with six wins, two draws and two defeats, leaving them behind only Paris Saint-Germain on 23 points and Lille on 21 on the Ligue 1 table before the leaders play on Saturday.

Liam Rosenior was appointed on July 7 on a contract running to June 2028, after a 107-day spell at Chelsea that ended with his sacking in April, and his side have scored 17 goals and conceded 10.

The standout figure is Lassine Sinayoko, who joined from Auxerre in the summer and leads the division with nine goals in 10 league games, three of them penalties, to go with five assists.

Sinayoko scored a hat-trick in the 3-2 win at Marseille on matchday three, added two goals and an assist in the 3-1 victory over Monaco on November 1, and then scored the only goal at his former club Auxerre on November 7, with Pablo Pagis providing the pass.

Jean Bouin has been the foundation of the season, as Paris FC are unbeaten at home in the league with four wins and a goalless draw against Lyon, scoring 12 goals and conceding five, and they have now gone seven consecutive matches there without defeat.

Their two league defeats came at Lorient (1-0 on October 10) and Lens (2-1 on October 24), and Rosenior said after the Lorient game that his players had never faced such a low block, which is the one test Angers could realistically set.

Angers have eight points from 10 games after two wins, two draws and six defeats, which leaves them six points clear of bottom side Le Havre, who have lost seven in a row.

Their wins came in a 3-1 victory at Auxerre on August 29 and a 2-0 home win over Troyes on September 19, and since the Troyes game they have drawn 0-0 with Lorient and lost four of five, scoring three goals and conceding 14.

The damage was done by two heavy defeats in a short space of time, a 5-1 loss at Brest on October 10, when Brest posted an expected-goals figure of 3.71 against Angers’ 1.39 and Jordan Lefort was sent off, and a 5-2 home defeat against Marseille on October 18.

The 2-0 loss at home to Nice on November 8 was a different problem, as Sofiane Diop scored in the second minute and Angers created so little that goalkeeper Anthony Lopes, a 35-year-old who joined after Nantes were relegated, needed six saves to prevent a heavier scoreline.

Stephane Gilli returns to the club he coached from July 2023 until his dismissal on February 22, when Paris FC were 15th, and he was appointed by Angers on June 9 on a deal to 2028 after Alexandre Dujeux left for Lorient.

Gilli has said Angers will adjust defensively without changing everything and that emotion will play no part on Sunday, but his attack has failed to score in five of 10 league matches, with Prosper Peter scoring against Troyes and Brest and Amine El Ouazzani against Troyes.

Paris FC will be without Jonathan Ikone, who has a dead leg, and Nhoa Sangui, who has a muscle injury, and neither is expected back until late November, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Samir Chergui (knock) are doubts.

Rosenior otherwise has a near-complete squad, and at Auxerre he used a back three of Hamari Traore, Otavio and Diego Coppola, with Coppola rated the man of the match by Maxifoot.

Moses Simon and Rudy Matondo provided the width at Auxerre, with Ilan Kebbal and Pagis supporting Sinayoko, who is expected to lead the line again.

Angers will be without Lefort, who is suspended, and Bane Diatta, who is injured, while Oumar Pona was ruled out after falling ill on his return from Mali Under-23 duty.

El Ouazzani is available after returning from injury, and Ousmane Camara and Amine Sbai both took part in training on Friday after being rested on Thursday.

With Lefort suspended, Emmanuel Biumla is expected to partner Camara in central defence, with Carlens Arcus and Kalulu at full-back in front of Lopes.

Paris FC possible starting lineup:.

Trapp; Traore, Otavio, Coppola; Simon, Lopez, Lees-Melou, Matondo; Kebbal, Pagis; Sinayoko.

Angers possible starting lineup:.

Lopes; Arcus, Camara, Biumla, Kalulu; Belkhdim, Belkebla; Allevinah, van den Boomen, Sbai; Peter.

Paris FC have scored 12 goals in five home league matches while Angers have conceded 14 in their last five, and that gap in output makes a home win the logical outcome.

Sinayoko decided the last two league wins, with two goals against Monaco and the winner at Auxerre, and an Angers back line without Lefort will have to deal with him for 90 minutes.

The counter-argument is that Angers beat Paris FC 1-0 in August 2025 and held them 0-0 at Jean Bouin in January, and that Rosenior’s side needed until the 63rd minute to break down a 5-4-1 Auxerre.

Those meetings, however, came when Gilli was still in the Paris FC dugout, and this Angers side has been opened up repeatedly at Brest and Marseille and has scored only three goals in five games.

Lopes should keep the margin respectable, but a side that has failed to score in five of 10 league games is more likely to be shut out than to find a way past Kevin Trapp.

Matthias Jaissle believes he saw "Newcastle United DNA-par excellence" in their second-half display against Arsenal.

Sources indicate that the Magpies held the Gunners to a 2-2 draw at St. James' Park on Saturday, after recovering from a dismal first-half performance.

After Eberechi Eze gave Arsenal a 1-0 lead at the break, Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw turned things around for Newcastle, though Noni Madueke salvaged a draw for the reigning champions.

Newcastle had just three shots (none on target), one touch in the opposition’s box, and won 46% of their duels during the first half, while facing 11 shots themselves (three on target).

In the second half, they had nine shots (three on target), 14 touches in the opposition box, and won 52.5% of their duels, facing just two shots from Arsenal (one on target).

Barnes' equaliser was the first goal the Gunners have conceded when leading in the Premier League this season, and Jaissle was delighted with how his players responded after the break.

The 25-year-old was deemed fit enough to start against Leeds, but was on the end of a number of heavy challenges early on at Stamford Bridge, including an incident which saw him require treatment after landing awkwardly on his back.

But their limitations in attack were again exposed on Tyneside. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring on the night with Noni Madueke impressing on the right with Bukayo Saka out injured but the visitors were short on inspiration off the bench.

Arsenal are interested in signing RB Leipzig star Nusa who is enjoying a superb season with the German club, with seven goals and eight assists in 16 appearances.

Leipzig have put a huge €80million (£67m) price tag on the Norway international who operates on the left for club and country.

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:10 EST, 20 November 2026.

While thinking over the last few days about his first press conference as Manchester United boss, Mauricio Pochettino would not have expected drones and the new Grand Theft Auto video game to be top of the agenda.

Having touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, taking a private jet laid on by United in the immediate aftermath of the United States’ game in Cincinnati against Haiti, it has been a whirlwind 48 hours for Pochettino and his staff.

On Thursday, he took charge of training for the first time against the backdrop of question marks around Bryan Mbeumo’s decision to post late into the night about popular fresh video game GTA VI.

By the time the day ended, the issue at hand was far more pressing as a drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Pochettino’s first session at Carrington.

How worried Pochettino actually is about the footage – which has since been pulled from YouTube, with a grovelling apology issued – remains to be seen but only this summer did the Argentine concede that ‘we are in an era of spies’.

The footage wasn’t a tactical golden ticket for Liverpool, but what was there to take from it?

A drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager.

The players get to work, with United's coaching staff seemingly unaware that their every move is being followed from the skies.

Pochettino sides have had a consistent set-up with and without the ball over the years.

The Argentine and his staff have, more often than not, leaned into a back-three in possession, shifting to a back-four without the ball.

In the drone footage we could see the United squad divided into three groups with one XI out on a different training pitch with Pochettino and coach Toni Jimenez.

That group were lined up in what appeared to be that preferred in-possession set-up, with academy defender Reece Munro tucking in from right back to form a back-three alongside Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven, traditional centre backs in a back-four.

Pochettino likes to have at least one full back push on extremely high to provide the width and in this snippet of his first training session, that responsibility landed on the shoulders of teenager Harry Amass, who has struggled for minutes this season, getting a total of just 29 under Michael Carrick.

The United players are put into position by Pochettino at Carrington.

Similarly, Pochettino has often shown a desire to play No 10s – or attacking midfielders – quite narrow. And that is what we saw here, with Amass and Mbeumo providing the width. Mbeumo was on the right of a 4-2-3-1 shape with Matheus Cunha and 17-year-old academy talent Jaume Camacho playing narrower and Joshua Zirkzee up front.

The formation becomes a 3-2-4-1 in possession with the full back pushing on to the wing, creating two No 10s behind the lone striker.

The footage was significant in that it revealed Pochettino is implementing his ideas from day one and is wasting no time in trying to embed a style he needs players to get up to speed with rapidly.

But little should be read into the personnel given it was an amalgamation of young players and senior regulars.

We could see academy players Amass, Camacho and Munro among the 10 outfield players, along with Cunha, Heaven, Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Zirkzee.

Of the 10 that were put to task by Pochettino, only four have started more than five league games this season.

It is highly improbable that the personnel used will be anywhere close to the starting XI at Anfield on Sunday.

The footage also indicated games of one-touch rondos going on between the two other groups which were divided between the rest of Pochettino’s coaching team, which includes his son Sebastiano and Miguel D’Agostino, as well as trusted assistant Jesus Perez.

Pochettino greets his latest players including Bryan Mbeumo, who lined up out wide in the first training session.

United's players start a 'rondo', where one defender stands in the middle and tries to pinch the ball from the players stood around the edge - who are allowed one touch at a time.

Sources indicate that one group included Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui. The other was academy-led with Bruno Fernandes leading a rondo that featured Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Dan Armer, as well as Jaydan Kamason.

But the use of Mbeumo in Pochettino’s work was one of the most interesting aspects, largely because he was back operating in a wider role.

With injuries hampering Benjamin Sesko, Mbeumo has had to spend a lot of the season deployed through the middle. That could well have to continue given Sesko is not anticipated to return until late January, but Pochettino’s decision to use Zirkzee as the figurehead in his set-up was intriguing.

Pochettino’s principles and set-up won’t vary too much; the onus now is on players to adapt. But Pochettino and Jimenez did look to have players in the correct positions. There were no obvious experiments – which makes sense when time is of the essence.

Amass plays off the left, Munro is a centre back, Maguire is comfortable in the middle of any back three, Camacho plays as a No 10 in the academy, both Mainoo and Santos have played together in a double pivot at the base of midfield and Zirkzee is a centre forward.

Pochettino likes a centre forward who can drop in to allow No 10s to run beyond and that suits Zirkzee’s style well, allowing him to be involved as a link man and not isolated with his back to goal.

Mbeumo works better running in behind as a counter-attacking striker, playing on the shoulder of the last defender.

How Pochettino uses Mbeumo over the longer term remains curious because swap out Camacho for Fernandes and Amass for Dorgu and there is a plausible set-up for success, with Mbeumo holding width on the right, Cunha and Fernandes in those central pockets they crave most, and Dorgu holding width off the left.

Lisandro Martinez (left) and Leny Yoro also meet Pochettino and his staff at Carrington.

Pochettino’s track record of working with and improving young players became immediately apparent, with so many given an introduction to his staff and their methods on day one.

While both Jack and Tyler Fletcher, along with Amass, Lacey and Bendito Mantato have made their first-team debuts, it was a golden opportunity in particular for Camacho, the stand-out player in the academy this season following the exit of JJ Gabriel.

United routinely promote multiple academy players each day to bolster numbers in first-team training sessions and it’s a good way for staff to bridge the gap in speed, physicality and intensity between senior and youth football.

Every manager that comes in likes to take on a project and when Ruben Amorim walked through the door it was Godwill Kukonki that caught the eye of staff.

Gabriel became a training mainstay in the months prior to his bombshell request to terminate his contract, and now Camacho, Munro and Armer are working towards first-team debuts instead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham winger Savio returned from injury on Saturday and almost immediately suffered the same injury that had just kept him out for six weeks.

Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in north London, thanks to goals from teenager Luca Williams-Barnett on his first Premier League start and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham climbed to ninth with the win, but there was disappointing news for them as Savio came off the bench in the second half but did not make the final whistle.

The summer-signing from Manchester City had not played since the draw with Manchester United on October 10 and may now face a similar period on the sidelines after a recurrence of the same hamstring problem.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: ‘I’m sorry for Savio’s injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him.

‘He’s a crucial player for us. He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season.’.

The 22-year-old joined from Manchester City for an initial £75 million and scored on his debut in a League Cup win over Charlton Athletic, but has not done much of note since then, hampered by injury.

The emergence of Williams-Barnett is much better news for De Zerbi, who has not been shy in talking up the talents of the 18-year-old who has come through the youth ranks at Spurs.

Sources indicate that ‘Luca is a special player,’ said the Italian. ‘I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He’s lucky because he’s playing in a top club with top team-mates.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my strategy, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

‘The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

‘And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

‘Even if they are Ballon d’Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.’.

De Zerbi, who was serving a touchline suspension against Ipswich, was asked if Williams-Barnett could reach the levels of the superstars he mentioned and said: ‘Yes, I think so.

‘And one of the best things in my career… I’ve seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

‘I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?’.

Spurs have now won four of their last five Premier League games and ended Saturday just three points adrift of Bournemouth in fourth.

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In a recent development, in short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

According to recent reports, krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

According to recent reports, “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche mentioned upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

It has been revealed that the club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

According to recent reports, milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Industry observers note that krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

Bruno Fernandes has left his Manchester United future up in the air, confirming that he has been offered a latest contract but there are no negotiations ongoing.

The 32-year-old is into the final few months of his current deal, which runs out at the end of the season, although the club has the option to extend it for another 12 months.

The Portugal international has been an integral figure since joining from Sporting in January 2020 and Manchester United want to keep him, having made offers of a upcoming deal.

Fernandes is not ready to commit just yet, leaving his options open for now after Mauricio Pochettino arrived this week to replace Michael Carrick as manager.

The Red Devils captain has dismissed the idea that he is holding out for more money or a longer contract, but does not feel the time is right to discuss terms.

‘No, there’s no negotiations ongoing,’ he told Sky Sports. ‘But I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United.

‘I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

It has been revealed that ‘Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I’ve always revealed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always mentioned, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, “Bruno, it’s time to part ways”, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.

‘Yeah, the club offered me a upcoming contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.’.

Fernandes’ future will, at least in part, be down to the opinion of Pochettino, who is tasked with rebuilding the Manchester United team into a successful one.

The Argentine takes charge of the Red Devils for the first time on Sunday as they travel to face Liverpool and Fernandes has liked what he has seen already from his new boss.

‘He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, stated it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,’ said the Portuguese.

‘He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.’.

After being attended to by the club’s medical team, Savio was replaced by Archie Gray to see out the 2-0 win over Ipswich.

It is not absolutely clear how long Savio will now be sidelined, with Tottenham next in action away at Sunderland next Sunday.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mikel Arteta was left sweating over the fitness of goalkeeper David Raya after the Arsenal shot-stopper was forced off in Saturday's 2-2 draw against Newcastle United.

Raya was replaced in the 70th minute by Kepa Arrizabalaga at St. James' Park after clutching his left arm and looking in some discomfort after a challenge with William Osula.

By the time Raya was replaced, Arsenal found themselves 2-1 down after goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw overturned Eberechi Eze's 33rd-minute opener.

However, Arsenal hit back 12 minutes from time through Noni Madueke, ensuring they remained six points clear of second-place Brighton at the top of the Premier League.

Arteta, however, remained concerned about the fitness of his goalkeeper, who has kept the joint-most clean sheets (seven, level with Bart Verbruggen) in the league this season.

The Gunners face Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Enzo Maresca's Manchester City to the Emirates Stadium five days later.

"Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news, and he will get assessed now," Arteta said of Raya's injury.

"He will probably get an MRI scan tomorrow, to see what exactly it is. At the moment, I don't know.".

Arsenal's result saw them end a 21-game run of Premier League games without a draw (W18 D3) since a 2-2 draw with Wolves back in February.

In an entertaining affair in the second half, Arsenal were edged in the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 1.48 to Newcastle's 1.73 from one fewer attempt (12 to 13).

Newcastle had just three shots (0 on target), one touch in the opposition’s box, and won 46% of their duels in the first half, while facing 11 shots themselves (three on target).

In the second half, they had nine shots (three on target), 14 touches in the opposition’s box, and won 52.5% of their duels, facing just two shots from Arsenal (one on target).

Recent findings suggest that and Arteta was left to rue a glut of chances while Arsenal were on top in the first half, conceding: "My feeling is that we have lost two points today. I say 'we', because we were exceptional in the first half.

"The level of aggression and intensity we put into the defensive aspect, the quality we demonstrated with the clarity to understand the jumps and the way they were making every adjustment man-to-man, the aggression to attack the right spaces, and we should have been three or four up.

"When you don't do that, then in the second half, you know the opponents will try to react, and that’s what they did to us.

"You have to increase the level to cope with that, rather than stay at the same level. Right from the beginning, we're not at the races – we start to lose duels, start to lose second balls, we give the ball away and have really bad circulation balls against their press, and we give them belief.

"We did both, giving them a goal from a throw-in that was very disappointing, and then we gave them a corner, and left their best set-piece player free – we get punished.

"After that, we came back to being that exceptional team; we could break the press, run, create infinite situations where we could score a goal, we scored the second one, and we had infinite situations with overloads to go and kill the game and win it.

"We lacked that moment of magic to win the game in the end.".

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:48.

Bayern Munich and England star Harry Kane has vowed to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing ankle surgery.

The striker sustained an ankle ligament injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw against FC Koln on Friday evening.

Kane attempted to carry on after being caught in a tackle from Koln defender Joel Schmied before he received treatment and made way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute.

Bayern released a statement after the game, revealing Kane would be out for a "few months" with a "torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle".

In a recent development, in a fresh update on Saturday morning, Bayern mentioned: "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight following the syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle, which he sustained in yesterday’s Bundesliga match against 1. FC Köln.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program.".

Kane also shared a defiant message on social media, accompanied by an image of him sitting on a hospital bed with his left foot in a protective boot.

Recent findings suggest that "The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

“‘Tough times don’t last, tough people do’ - my guy Julian Edelman (three-time Super Bowl winner) told me this one!

According to recent reports, “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!”.

The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” - my guy @Edelman11 told me this one! Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut! ❤️?

With Kane likely to be out until the end of February, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany will have to come up with solutions to negate the impact of being without his star striker.

Ismael Saibari can play as a centre-forward, but he is right now sidelined with the same injury as Kane, putting him out of action until the start of February.

Serge Gnabry is also on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back until the turn of the year, leaving Kompany without another potential candidate to fill the void created by Kane's absence.

Noah Codjo-Evora is an option if Kompany decides to put his faith in youth, but the 19-year-old is unlikely to start regularly given the fact he only made his first-team debut as a substitute on Friday.

That means Kompany will likely opt to field a false nine in the coming weeks and months, which is a role Lennart Karl played when Kane went off against Koln.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It has been revealed that it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

Sources indicate that if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Published: 05:49 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 20 November 2026.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: 'Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

'In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.' District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but later signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

The court had heard Mr Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

Mark Mogan (right) has been found not guilty of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo (left) after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

He was alleged to have said: 'Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black b*****d.'.

Opening the case last month, Mr Jones mentioned: 'That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

'Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had noted.' Mr Mogan then shouted "I'm talking to you, you ****", the court heard.

Witnesses also noted they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mr Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mr Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to 'hurry up'.

Mr Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

Semenyo, who scored a brace in the game, had brought the incident to the attention of match referee Anthony Taylor and the match was briefly halted while both managers and captains were spoken to.

At half time an announcement was made to the crowd asking for no racist abuse and pictures on social media showed a man in a wheelchair being escorted along the touchline and out of the ground.

Mogan, pictured with Liverpool legend Robbie Fowler, would have been banned for life if he'd have been found guilty.

Merseyside Police later announced the man had been arrested and then was bailed for three months pending further investigations.

Pictures on social media revealed Mogan playing wheelchair basketball for a team called the Greenbank Meteors while other images show him posing with Liverpool legends Robbie Fowler and Emile Heskey.

After he was charged, Liverpool confirmed he would be banned for life if found guilty but Judge Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty on Friday morning.

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • Recent findings suggest that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • It has been revealed that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

Recent findings suggest that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

It has been revealed that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of new electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

According to recent reports, here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

In such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Industry observers note that our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

Sources indicate that for either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

a, Schematic representation of the full phase diagram formed in our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN system. External parameters (such as carrier density n, magnetic field B and temperature T) define one coordinate axis, whereas the intrinsic stacking order of the sandwich heterostructure defines the other. Two local energy minima exist corresponding to AA and AB stacking configurations, with their dominant stackings shown in c and d, respectively. Blue and red arrows indicate transitions between these configurations; solid arrows denote states realized under continuous tuning of external parameters, whereas dashed arrows mark the abrupt structural phase transition, matching the solid and dashed lines in the experiments shown in Fig. 3a–c. b, Moiré-induced corrugation observed in a double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN device, measured at room temperature by AFM. Inset shows the corrugation profile along the light blue line. Phonon squeezing reduces corrugation at low temperatures. The unit cell outlined in black matches that in g. c,d, Schematic illustrations of the competing sandwich configurations at double-aligned interfaces: AB (c) and AA (d) stacking configurations. e–h, MD simulations of strain distributions. Panels g and h show our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN configurations with AB and AA stacking configurations, respectively, and panels e and f show reference calculations for double-aligned hBN/graphene/hBN configurations. Comparison highlights the notable role of mhBN on strain enhancement, leading to much stronger reconstruction patterns—triangular and hexagonal reconstructions, respectively. Dashed circles indicate vertices of domains arising from these two reconstruction types, on which strain-induced PLLs develop, as shown on the right. The yellow-to-orange gradient bar indicates increasing strain amplitude. i, The theoretical calculated corrugation of the graphene–hBN interface as a function of the twist angle.

Unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering upcoming phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

Industry observers note that we emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

It has been revealed that two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

Recent findings suggest that a, Schematic of the transport device with hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN heterostructure (inset) in a dual-graphite gate configuration. b, Schematic of the mhBN/graphene/hBN transport device. The unencapsulated mhBN enables AFM measurement. Inset, AFM image of the device (bottom right) and its fast Fourier transform (FFT). The FFT confirms the double alignment and gives the periods of both superlattices, which agree well with those derived from the transport measurement in d. Scale bar, 50 nm. c,d, Longitudinal resistance Rxx of the states before (blue) and after (red) the transition in the device types in a and b, measured at T = 1.6 K. The neutrality point, labelled ‘NP’, shifts from no doping to n-doping (device in a) and from p-doping to n-doping (device in b) on transition. According to recent reports, for both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

In a recent development, first, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

In Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

By applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

In a recent development, note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

The phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a reveals that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

Figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g indicates zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Industry observers note that notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) shows that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

In Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

It has been revealed that the energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

It has been revealed that we now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

According to recent reports, the reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.
